title: How Pieter Levels built 12 startups in 12 months to ship fast and earn press
summary: Levels explains why he builds one minimal MVP per month after a two-year project flopped with four free trial users. The monthly deadline forces him to finish and keep scope small, and the 12-in-12 narrative earns press coverage that drives users. He also covers sourcing ideas from his own problems, funding bigger goals with side-project cash flow, and not being intimidated by polished products.

principles.text: Ship small products fast; a monthly deadline forces you to finish and keep scope minimal.
principles.quote: if I have to build something every month it forced me to finish it and it forced me to keep it minimal as well which I think is a good in terms of an MVP right

principles.text: Long perfectionist builds often launch to nobody; shorten the loop to learn demand sooner.
principles.quote: after like two years I launched it and nobody was using it there was just like there's like four free trial users using it and they left

principles.text: Press wants news; build a narrative around your products or personality that fits you, and use press to get users.
principles.quote: you need to think of a narrative around your products or around your personality I guess um that fits your personality as well because you you can't fake it right

principles.text: Build products that solve a problem you have yourself, and borrow proven layouts for inspiration.
principles.quote: I get an ID from probably some problem I have myself like with Nomad list I had the problem where I didn't really know which cities to go to

principles.text: Ideas are common; execution is what differentiates, so keep a backlog and ship.
principles.quote: I think we all have the same ideas and it's just about execution now

principles.text: Use side projects for monthly cash flow to fund working on bigger problems later.
principles.quote: you need cash flow to solve big problems right most of the times so if you if you're in a nine-to-five job and you want to solve big problems I guess a good Avenue would be to build your own stuff that gives you cash flow monthly
